title: Optimizing parameters for multiband ABRs to continuous speech
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings used to optimize parameters for measuring multiband auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) to continuous peaky speech. It includes two experiments: one examining the effect of stimulus phase profile (zero vs. chirp) on ABR amplitude, and another examining the effect of narrator fundamental frequency (f0) on ABR responses. The data support investigations into efficient, naturalistic methods for measuring subcortical auditory responses using continuous speech stimuli.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from participants seated in a darkened sound-isolating booth listening to continuous audiobook stimuli (peaky speech) presented at 65 dB SPL and 48 kHz sampling rate through ER-2 insert earphones connected to an RME Digiface USB sound card. Custom Python scripts using expyfun controlled stimulus presentation. Raw EEG was recorded in Brain Products BrainVision format (.eeg, .vhdr, .vmrk), with stimulus and regressor files stored in .hdf5 format for deconvolution analyses.
